$comment: Every stat the framework itself owns: what it wraps, where it lives, what it does, what
the game authored, and who reads it. Ids derive from the framework's reserved owner
string 'ectype' and the name (MD5 of 'ectype:stat:ectype/<name>', low 28 bits under
0x20000000); they are also rows in stat-names.csv, which is the perk builder's alias
list. The declaration is src/FrameworkStats.cs; the wiring is the file named in
'wiredBy'. Authored values are the prefab's as read at wiring time and logged at spawn
('grapple stat surface installed' / 'character stat surface installed'); re-check them
after a game update. 'mechanism' says how the game consumes the number, so a reader
can predict what a modifier does without opening the decompile.
'authoredVerified' is false where the value is the Opsive/class default rather than one read back from a spawn log; replace it with the logged number after the first run.

stats.name: GrapplingHookFlightSpeed
stats.collection: the hook ability's own StatTagCollection (child of the player's)
stats.mechanism: Speed the hook head is launched at toward the aim point. Higher reaches the anchor sooner; range is a separate vanilla stat (GrapplingHookRange).
consumers: perk StatMods targeting character (recurse into the ability's collection)

stats.name: GrapplingHookPullSpeed
stats.mechanism: Cap on the character's speed along the line while being pulled. Read per tick inside the pull update, which is why the field stays the sink.

stats.name: GrapplingHookPullAcceleration
stats.mechanism: Acceleration applied toward the anchor each tick until pull speed is reached. Read per tick.

stats.name: GrapplingHookMissCooldown
stats.mechanism: Cooldown applied instead of the full one when the hook attaches to nothing.

stats.name: GrapplingHookCooldown
stats.wraps: ChannelGrapplingHook.CooldownSeconds - the SAME ModifiableFloat the base class registers as ClassAbilityCooldown, under a second id
stats.mechanism: No write-back, no field: a hook-scoped alias so a cooldown perk can target the grapple alone. A modifier against the vanilla ClassAbilityCooldown alias reaches every ability on the character.

stats.name: ExternalForceDamping
stats.mechanism: Every tick the locomotion divides its external-force velocity by (1 + ExternalForceDamping * timeScale * ExternalForceDampingMultiplier). The jetpack moves the character exclusively through AddForce into that channel, so this is how long EVA momentum persists. 0 is fully Newtonian and plays as uncontrollable; the Skirmisher's Thruster Suit cuts it to x0.1 for its channel.
consumers: ectype-skirmisher ThrusterSuitAbility: ExponentialMultiplier (multiplier - 1) applied on channel start, removed by source on stop
gameplay/anthem-eva FlightState: ExponentialMultiplier (DampingScale - 1) applied while the Anthem flight model is engaged and the knob is off its sentinel, removed by source otherwise

stats.name: ExternalForceDampingTime
stats.mechanism: On leaving a moving platform's inertia zone into open space the game ramps ExternalForceDampingMultiplier from a curve over this many seconds, so the ship's velocity is kept rather than damped away at once. The ramp is scaled by the platform's exit speed: full length at >= 20 m/s, none at <= 5 m/s, linear between. Longer keeps launch momentum longer.

stats.name: MotorDamping
stats.mechanism: Every tick the walking motor throttle is divided by (1 + MotorDamping * timeScale). With MotorAcceleration it sets top walking speed (steady state where acceleration equals damping) and how fast you stop on release. Applies on foot inside gravity zones; the jetpack does not use the motor.

stats.name: MotorAcceleration
stats.wraps: Opsive CharacterLocomotion.MotorAcceleration (public Vector3 property over m_MotorAcceleration; the stat is its horizontal magnitude)
stats.units: throttle per tick (magnitude of the x/z pair)
stats.mechanism: Per-axis force the walking motor adds each tick, scaled by input and slope factor. The write-back multiplies the authored vector by (value / authored magnitude), so x and z keep their ratio and y stays 0. Raising it raises both responsiveness and top walking speed.

stats.name: GravityAmount
stats.units: velocity added per fixed tick, along GravityDirection
stats.mechanism: Accumulated into the character's downward velocity every fixed update while UseGravity is on (inside a gravity zone). Only the strength; whether gravity applies at all is the zone's decision and is untouched. UltimateCharacterLocomotion.ResetCharacter zeroes the field, but nothing calls it.

stats.name: IncomingProjectileSpeed
stats.wraps: no field: a factor read by a consumer that puts an ExponentialMultiplier of (factor - 1) on each hostile SyncedProjectile's own Speed stat
stats.wiredBy: src/ShipStats.cs, PlayerControlledShip.RegisterStats postfix; consumer is a SyncedProjectilesSynchronizer.RegisterNpcProjectile postfix plus a re-apply over in-flight shots on every change
stats.mechanism: NPC shots move Speed.Value * fixedDeltaTime each tick and expire at Range / Speed, both read live, so a factor below 1 slows shots in flight and still lets them reach full range. The consumer also rescales the shot's Velocity snapshot, which sizes the collision sweep. Only shots whose Faction the ship counts as enemy are touched, so the ship's own missiles are not. Hitscan RayProjectiles ignore speed; LegacyWeaponProjectile and composite WeaponProjectile are not covered.
consumers: perk StatMods targeting seatShip (applied on every client for every seated player, which keeps each client's simulation of the shot in step)

stats.name: HandAttractorMaxRange
stats.wraps: no field: the ModifiableFloat a hand-attractor ability reads as its capture range
stats.collection: the owning class ability's own StatTagCollection (child of the player's)
stats.wiredBy: src/HandAttractorStats.cs, called from the ability's Awake
stats.mechanism: Radius of the capture cone and leash on the held target. Each float is registered twice in the owning ability's collection: under this id and under the vanilla ship-attractor id it mirrors, so a character-side modifier on either lands on the one float (StatTagCollection.ApplyModifier matches Type against every Stats key). A source names one of the two ids, never both, or the two modifiers compound. Ship-collection sources (seatShip perks, ship-installed items) do not reach it. Mirrors AttractorMaxRange.

stats.name: HandAttractorPullVelocity
stats.wraps: no field: the ModifiableFloat a hand-attractor ability writes into the target's CarryableObject.Velocity each frame
stats.collection: the owning class ability's own StatTagCollection (child of the player's)
stats.wiredBy: src/HandAttractorStats.cs, called from the ability's Awake
stats.mechanism: Pull speed toward the emit point, braked linearly inside 3 m. Each float is registered twice in the owning ability's collection: under this id and under the vanilla ship-attractor id it mirrors, so a character-side modifier on either lands on the one float (StatTagCollection.ApplyModifier matches Type against every Stats key). A source names one of the two ids, never both, or the two modifiers compound. Ship-collection sources (seatShip perks, ship-installed items) do not reach it. Mirrors AttractorPullVelocity.

stats.name: HandAttractorDuration
stats.wraps: FiniteDurationClassAbility.FiniteTimeDuration of the owning hand-attractor ability (already registered by the game as ClassAbilityDuration)
stats.collection: the owning class ability's own StatTagCollection (child of the player's)
stats.wiredBy: src/HandAttractorStats.cs RegisterTiming, called from the ability's Awake
stats.mechanism: A second id onto the same ModifiableFloat the game registers as ClassAbilityDuration; AbilityStarted copies FiniteTimeDuration.Value into CurrentActiveDuration, so a modifier here sets the next channel's length with no code on that path. Scoped to the hand, where ClassAbilityDuration reaches every class ability on the character. A source names one of the two ids, never both, or they compound. Registered by HandAttractorStats.RegisterTiming into the owning ability's collection. Ship-collection sources (seatShip perks, ship-installed items) do not reach it. Authored value is the ability's DurationSeconds config.

stats.name: HandAttractorCooldown
stats.wraps: ClassAbility.CooldownSeconds of the owning hand-attractor ability (already registered by the game as ClassAbilityCooldown)
stats.collection: the owning class ability's own StatTagCollection (child of the player's)
stats.wiredBy: src/HandAttractorStats.cs RegisterTiming, called from the ability's Awake
stats.mechanism: A second id onto the same ModifiableFloat the game registers as ClassAbilityCooldown; ClassAbility.GoOnCooldown sets CurrentCooldown = CooldownSeconds.Value, so a modifier here sets the next cooldown with no code on that path. Scoped to the hand, where ClassAbilityCooldown reaches every class ability on the character. A source names one of the two ids, never both, or they compound. Registered by HandAttractorStats.RegisterTiming into the owning ability's collection. Ship-collection sources (seatShip perks, ship-installed items) do not reach it. Authored value is the ability's CooldownSeconds config.

stats.name: HandAttractorBeams
stats.wraps: no field: the ModifiableFloat a hand-attractor ability reads as how many items one channel holds
stats.collection: the owning class ability's own StatTagCollection (child of the player's)
stats.wiredBy: src/HandAttractorStats.cs RegisterTiming, called from the ability's Awake
stats.mechanism: Read once at each channel start. No vanilla mirror. Use flat modifiers: +1 is one more beam. Registered by HandAttractorStats.RegisterTiming into the owning ability's collection. Ship-collection sources (seatShip perks, ship-installed items) do not reach it. Authored value is the ability's Beams config.

stats.name: ModuleInstallSpeed
stats.wraps: no field: a factor on the progress clock (BuildProcess.StateTimer) of an install, uninstall or upgrade the player started
stats.wiredBy: src/BuildStats.cs; registered by the Player.Awake postfix, consumed by a BuildProcess.Run prefix
stats.mechanism: The master runs every BuildProcess; each Run adds deltaTime to StateTimer, which SetState zeroes on every state change. Working completes when it reaches GameConfiguration.BuildBoxConstructDuration (install) or DeconstructDuration (uninstall and upgrade) - 10 s and 5 s as code defaults; the shipped asset's values are not read back - and Completing (the fold, the module already built or removed) at a literal 3.25 s. Those are one shared value for the room, so the consumer adds deltaTime * (factor - 1) to the clock of each ConstructionProcess, DeconstructionProcess or UpgradeProcess in Working or Completing instead, reading the factor from the player named by the process's RequesterActorId: the one who socketed the build box, pressed uninstall or used the upgrader. +40% percent is 1.4x the rate, so the job takes 1/1.4 of its time. The 1 s placement check (Waiting) is untouched. Two client-side visuals keep stock speed: the build box's progress diodes (started with the stock duration, short of full when the module appears) and its fold animation, which an install cuts short when the master destroys the box at 3.25 s / factor.
consumers: perk StatMods targeting character (the master carries every player's)

stats.name: ShipDrag
stats.wraps: MovingSpacePlatform.PhysicalData.Friction (public float in the public SpacePlatformData struct field on the player ship root)
stats.wiredBy: src/ShipPlatformStats.cs, called from the PlayerControlledShip.RegisterStats postfix in src/ShipStats.cs; the platform is read with GetComponent because Platform is assigned after RegisterStats runs
stats.units: quadratic drag coefficient (floored at 1% of authored)
stats.mechanism: MovingSpacePlatform.ApplyFriction runs every FixedUpdate on every machine, with no ownership gate, and moves the velocity toward zero by speed^2 * Friction * dt / Mass, with speed floored at MinVelocityFriction (20 m/s authored) on any tick nobody thrusts. Full-thrust top speed is sqrt(EngineThrustPower * EnginePower * ForwardPower / Friction), so a factor f on the stat scales top speed by 1/sqrt(f) on every axis and weakens coasting drag and braking by f. No IL stores to PhysicalData, and the only store to Friction is the struct's constructor, so seeding once is sound. Other readers: ShipPilotHelper.MaxVelocity, read live by CruiseControlModule.EnableCruiseControl when cruise engages (engaged under a cut, it can lock a speed the engine cannot hold once the cut ends, and the locked speed then decays to the normal cap) and latched at Start by ShipAutoTilt for its pitch and roll scaling; SignatureComponent latches sqrt(EngineThrustPower / Friction) at Start as the speed of full movement signature, so speed above it evaluates the signature curve past 1. PilotAid does not read it: its auto-brake is a thrust input scaled by ForwardPower, so a cut leaves the aid's braking authority unchanged while drag's own braking weakens. Stat changes are not replicated; the helm owner (the master while the helm is empty) is authoritative for the platform and every other machine extrapolates with its own drag between snapshots, so a contribution belongs on every machine. Authored value decoded from the four player ship prefabs (Frigate, Frigate Awakening, Destroyer, Striker), not yet read back from a spawn log.
consumers: perk StatMods targeting seatShip or characterShip (applied on every client)
ShipSpeedSurge (src/ShipSpeedSurge.cs): ExponentialMultiplier of (1/s^2 - 1), s = 1 + magnitude * (1 - progress), through TimedStatContributions on every machine
